newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: SUPER LEAGUE GIVEN THE GO AHEAD
News Limited has won its appeal against the ruling blocking the Super League competition from beginning until the year two thousand.
The ruling has been overturned by a full bench of the Federal Court.
Three senior judges have reached the unanimous decision that the landmark Super League judgment handed down by Justice James Burchett in February should be set aside.
The full bench says on many issues its drawn different conclusions to Justice Burchett.
ALP DENIES DEAL WITH AUSTRALIANS AGAINST FURTHER IMMIGRATION
The ALP has denied accusations by the Liberal Party that it made a deal with the Australians Against Further Immigration party for the federal by-election in the western Sydney seat of Lindsay.
Labor Party secretary Gary Gray says the ALP hasn't made a deal to swap preferences with AAFI in the by-election.
Mr Gray says the Liberals are probably just angry because the AAFI usually gives their preference to the Coaltion.
He says the Australians Against Further Immigration party makes its own decision about who it gives its preferences to.
ACCOUNTANTS URGE TAX REFORM
The Australian Society of Certified Practicing Accountants says tax reform is necessary for the benefit of both individual taxpayers and the economy.
Speaking at the National Tax Reform Summit in Canberra, the Society's Chris Knoblanche has described the current system as inefficient and unfriendly.
The Summit's also heard that the system promotes avoidance schemes and speculative investing, and discourages saving.
There has also been calls for the introduction of a GST to make the system fairer.
MURDDERER TO BE RELEASED AT MIDNIGHT
The murderer of South Coast teenager, Kim Barry, will be released from jail at midnight tonight, 14 years after being sentenced to life imprisonment.
The New South Wales Offender's Review Board has approved the release of Graham Gene Potter from Cooma jail under strict parole conditions.
Potter was sentenced in 1982 to life imprisonment but his sentence was reduced to a minimum of almost 13-years in 1993 under the former State Government's truth-in-sentencing legislation.
After being refused parole twice before, Potter will be set free at midnight, but will have on-going psychological assessment, and has been banned from contact with the victim's family.
AUSTRALIAN FESTIVAL IN CANBERRA
The nation's only festival of exclusively Australian works gets under way in Canberra tonight with a play based on the murder of New South wales teenager Leigh Leigh.
Blackrock, by Nick Enright will head the fortnight of the National Festival of Australian Theatre.
Other highlights include a preview of the new musical by Black Swan Theatre as well as work by Rock'n'Roll Circus; Legs on the Wall; and the new dance company Chunky Move.
Director Rob Brookman says the festival's devotion to Australian work makes it a special event on the arts calender.
CHILD PROTECTION TRANSFER PLAN
A meeting of Community Services Ministers in Melbourne has agreed to transfer Child Protection Proceedings across State and Territory borders.
The leaders say there has been problems in the past, when a child under a protection order moves to another state.
Queensland Community Services Minister Kev Lingard says under the new agreement, protection orders will be administered by the state where the child lives.
POET FINED $100
A Brisbane poet has been fined 100 dollars after being found guilty of exhibiting an obscene publication.
David Saywell had pleaded not guilty in the Brisbane Magistrates Court after he glued a poem to the Commonwealth bank in West End to advertise his talent.
But the police described the poem which contains the "F" word as obscene.
The Magistrate said it was on the very lowest end of the scale of obscenity and did not record a conviction.
